SECTION 3 – BOILER AND HEATING SYSTEM

3.1 General

The pavilion is heated by a Worcester Greenstar 24i combi boiler, installed in the plant cupboard off the main corridor. The boiler supplies radiators in the main hall, committee room, offices, and both changing rooms, and also provides hot water to the kitchen and toilets. The boiler is not to be touched by volunteers or visiting teams. Only the Facilities Officer, the club's named gas engineer, or a Gas Safe registered engineer may work on it.

The current gas engineer used by the club is P. Hensley (Merrowdale Heating Services), telephone 01305 749 118. He has serviced the boiler since 2018. The boiler service is due every September, before the heating season begins. The service record book is kept on the shelf above the boiler, in a clear plastic folder.

3.2 Boiler controls

The boiler has a simple dial thermostat on the wall of the main corridor, near the plant cupboard door. The dial is marked in numbers from 1 to 5, not in degrees. Normal winter setting is 3. Do not turn the dial above 4; the radiators in the main hall become too hot and the committee room overheats. In mild weather (October and April), setting 2 is usually enough.

There is a timer switch on the wall next to the thermostat. The timer is set as follows:

| Period | Setting |
|--------|---------|
| Weekdays, Sept–May | On 06:00–09:00 and 16:00–22:00 |
| Weekends and bank holidays, Sept–May | On 07:00–11:00 and 15:00–22:00 |
| June–August | Off, except when the hall is booked for events. For events, set to "On" manually and turn off at the end of the day. |

The timer is a mechanical type with pins. If the time shown is wrong after a power cut, reset it using the small dial behind the front cover. Do not force the pins; they are plastic and break easily. A replacement timer is kept in the plant cupboard, in the box marked "spares".

3.3 Pressure and bleeding

The boiler pressure gauge is on the front of the boiler, behind the drop-down flap. Normal pressure when the system is cold is between 1 and 1.5 bar. If the pressure drops below 1 bar, top up using the grey filling loop underneath the boiler. The filling loop valve should be closed again after topping up. If the pressure keeps dropping, do not keep topping up; report it to the Facilities Officer, as there may be a leak.

Radiators should be bled at the start of the heating season (usually the first week of October) and again in January if any radiator is cold at the top. Use the bleed key stored on the hook inside the plant cupboard door. Hold a cloth under the bleed valve before opening it, as water may spurt out. Close the valve as soon as water comes out steadily.

3.4 Fault finding and reporting

If the boiler fails to light, first check that the gas supply is on (the isolation valve on the pipe next to the boiler should be in line with the pipe) and that the timer is calling for heat. Then check the pressure gauge. If the boiler display shows an error code, note the code and the time it appeared, and call P. Hensley. Do not press the reset button more than twice in one day; repeated resetting can hide a real fault and may cause damage.

The following faults have been seen before and are noted here for reference:

| Fault | Likely cause | Action |
|-------|--------------|--------|
| Boiler lights, then goes out after a few minutes | Blocked condensate pipe (usually in cold weather) | Check the external pipe for ice; pour warm (not boiling) water over it. If it recurs, call the engineer. |
| Radiators hot at the bottom, cold at the top | Air in the system | Bleed the radiator. |
| Banging or gurgling noise from the boiler | Low pressure or trapped air | Check pressure; bleed radiators. If noise continues, call the engineer. |
| No hot water, but radiators heat up | Faulty diverter valve | Call the engineer. This has happened twice, in 2019 and 2020. |

**Section 4: Windows, Guttering and Pest Control**

**4.1 Window cleaning**

Windows at the pavilion are to be cleaned internally and externally at least once a month from March to October, and once every six weeks from November to February. The schedule is set out in the Facilities calendar on the noticeboard in the plant cupboard.

Use the following products, stored in the locked cleaning cupboard in the annex:

- Glass cleaner (supplied by County Supplies, order code GL-114)
- Microfibre cloths (blue for glass, yellow for frames)
- Squeegee with rubber blade (long handle for upper panes)

Do not use abrasive pads or any cleaner containing bleach on the aluminium frames. The frames are powder-coated and bleach will mark them. Where frames have been repainted (see note in Appendix C), use only the mild soap solution described in Section 2.4.

Ladder use: the step ladder in the store is for internal window cleaning only. The extension ladder is kept in the external store behind the kitchen door and must only be used by two people. One person to foot the ladder at all times. Do not work from the ladder at the top of the fire escape; the ground is uneven there and the ladder will not sit level. For the high window over the main entrance, use the window pole with the squeegee attachment rather than climbing.

Report any cracked or broken panes immediately to the Facilities Officer. Do not attempt to remove broken glass yourself. Temporary boarding is kept in the store (two sheets of 6mm ply, marked "WINDOW BOARD").

**4.2 Gutter clearance**

Gutters and downpipes are to be cleared of leaves and debris twice a year: once in late autumn (usually the second week of November) and once in early spring (usually the third week of March). The exact dates are set by the Grounds Staff and will be written in the weekly task list.

The spring clearance is the more important of the two. The oak tree by the car park drops catkins in early April, and these block the downpipe at the corner nearest the tree. If the downpipe blocks, water overflows and runs down the side of the pavilion wall, which has caused damp in the past.

Method:

1. From the ground, use the gutter scoop on the extending pole to remove loose debris.
2. For the sections above the flat roof of the annex, use the ladder from the external store. Do not stand on the flat roof; the felt is not rated for foot traffic.
3. Flush the downpipes with a hose from the top, checking that water runs freely from the outlet at ground level.
4. Check the outlet at ground level is clear of leaves and that the gully grid is in place.

If a downpipe is found to be cracked or leaking at a joint, mark the location with tape and report it. Do not attempt to seal leaks with silicone from the store; the correct repair is a new section of pipe, which the Facilities Officer will arrange.

The gutter above the kitchen has been repaired twice (2019 and 2020) at the joint near the extractor fan outlet. This joint is prone to working loose in high winds. Check this joint specifically at each clearance and after any storm with wind speeds above 40mph (the Met Office warnings are usually enough of a prompt).

**4.3 Pest control**

The pavilion has a pest control contract with Dorset Pest Services (contract number DPS-221, renewed annually in April). The contract covers the building interior and the immediate exterior, including the bin store.

Routine monitoring:

- Mouse traps are set in the plant cupboard, the kitchen, and the store room. These are checked weekly by the Cleaner (normally a Thursday). The Cleaner initials the trap check sheet, which is kept in the back of the cleaning folder.
- Wasp nests: if a nest is reported, do not attempt to remove it. The contractor will attend within 48 hours. The nest at the top of the fire escape (reported July 2020) was treated and removed; the wasps have not returned.
- Pigeons: the roof of the annex is a known roosting spot. The bird spikes on the annex roof edge were replaced in March 2021 and are holding up well. If pigeons are seen entering the roof void, report it; there is a gap in the soffit on the east side that the Facilities Officer has ordered a repair for.

Archive item 3: North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019
Source format: Maintenance Manual

The pitch is mown twice per week during the playing season, normally Tuesday and Friday
morning, weather permitting. Cut height is set at:

- Spring (March – May): 30mm
- Summer (June – August): 25mm
- Early autumn (September – October): 30mm

The final cut of the week (Friday) should be lower than the Tuesday cut by 2mm to allow for
growth over the weekend. If the pitch is waterlogged, do not mow. Mowing wet grass will
pull the sward and leave ruts.

Mowing pattern should alternate each cut:

- Week A: North–South (lengthways)
- Week B: East–West (widthways)

Do not mow the same direction twice in a row. This prevents grain and helps the grass stand
upright. The outfield (run-off) areas should be cut at 45mm, fortnightly.

2.2 Winter Mowing (November – February)

Mowing is reduced to once per week, or once every two weeks in very cold weather. Height is
raised to 40mm. Do not cut below 35mm during frost. If frost is forecast, stop mowing
48 hours beforehand where possible.

Winter mowing is for tidiness only – the grass will not be actively growing. If the pitch is
frozen solid, do not walk on it with mowers. Frost damage to the crown of the grass plant
can take until April to recover.

2.3 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.5 – "Spring cut 2019: started 12 March after dry week. J.B."
- p.5 – "Changed Friday cut to 28mm from 30mm on 3 May – grass growing fast. J.B."
- p.6 – "Winter cut 2018/19: only 14 cuts total. Mild but wet. J.B."

---

3. IRRIGATION SCHEDULE

3.1 Water Source and System

North Pitch is irrigated using a single pop-up sprinkler system fed from the club's borehole
(not the mains supply). The borehole is located behind the pavilion and is shared with the
bowls green. Water pressure varies with demand, so the sprinklers should not be run at the
same time as the bowls green irrigation.

The system has 12 pop-up heads, arranged in two banks of six. Bank A covers the northern
half, Bank B covers the southern half. Each bank runs for 20 minutes per cycle.

3.2 Irrigation Rules

North Pitch has_surface_type natural grass. Record status: current.

Irrigation is only permitted:

- Between 0600 and 0900 hours (to reduce evaporation)
- When the soil moisture deficit exceeds 15mm
- When wind speed is below 15 mph (check the anemometer at the pavilion)

Do not irrigate during rainfall or when rainfall is forecast within 6 hours. Do not irrigate
within 24 hours of a match unless the ground is exceptionally dry and the match official
has approved it.

3.3 Spring and Summer Schedule (April – September)

Irrigation is not usually required before mid-May unless there is a dry spell. The target is
to maintain moisture at a depth of 150mm. Use the soil probe to check – the top 25mm should
be dry but not dusty.

Typical schedule when irrigation is needed (dry spells only):

- Bank A: 0600, 0620, 0640 (20 min each)
- Bank B: 0700, 0720, 0740 (20 min each)

This gives a total of 60 minutes per bank per day, equivalent to approximately 8mm of
water. Do not exceed 12mm per day unless the pitch is newly seeded.

3.4 Autumn and Winter

Irrigation is stopped from October to March. The sprinkler heads must be drained and blown
through with compressed air before the first frost. This is a two-person job – see the
Winterisation Checklist (Appendix C).

3.5 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.9 – "Borehole pump replaced 14/05/19 – pressure much better. J.B."
- p.9 – "Irrigation needed only 4 times in June 2019 – wet month. J.B."
- p.10 – "Winterisation done 24/10/19. Heads drained OK. J.B."

---

4. FERTILIZER TYPES AND APPLICATION

4.1 General Principles

North Pitch receives three to four fertilizer applications per year. The aim is to maintain
a healthy sward without excessive growth. We do not use growth regulators – mowing is our
primary control.

All fertilizer must be stored in the locked chemical store (shed 2) and logged in the COSHH
register. Application records must be kept in the Fertilizer Log (Appendix D). Only
trained staff may apply fertilizer.
Second application is usually June, only if the sward looks pale or the match schedule is heavy. Use a low-nitrogen feed:

- Product: 5-0-10 with iron
- Rate: 20g/m²
- Spreader setting: 10

Do not apply during a heatwave – if the forecast is above 25°C, wait for cooler weather. The iron helps with moss suppression but can stain the mower decks, so wash down after use.

4.4 Autumn Application

Third application is September/October. This is the most important one for root growth over winter.

- Product: 10-0-20 (high potash)
- Rate: 30g/m²
- Spreader setting: 14

Apply before the end of October. If the ground is very wet, use the pedestrian spreader instead of the tractor-mounted one to avoid rutting.

4.5 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.12 – "Tried the 9-7-7 at 30g in April 2020 – too much, scorched the edges near the car park. Stick to 25g. J.B."
- p.12 – "June feed skipped in 2021 – pitch was green enough. Saved a bag. J.B."
- p.13 – "Autumn feed went on late 24/10/23 – fine, no frost yet. M.W."

---

5. MOWING PATTERNS AND HEIGHTS

5.1 General Principles

North Pitch is mown throughout the growing season, typically March to October. The aim is a playing surface of consistent height, with no scalping on the slopes and no build-up of thatch. All mowing must be recorded in the Mowing Log (Appendix E), including date, height, and any problems encountered.

Mowing heights are measured from the cutting edge to the ground, with the mower on a hard level surface. Check the height with a depth gauge before each mowing session – do not rely on the mower's own scale alone.

5.2 Spring Mowing Heights (March – May)

Spring mowing starts when the grass begins to grow, usually mid-March. Start higher than the summer height and reduce gradually as growth picks up.

- Early spring (March): 40mm
- Mid-spring (April): 38mm
- Late spring (May): 35mm

North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019 mowing_height_spring 35 mm. Record status: current. This is the standard spring height and is current – it has not changed since the manual was first issued. Do not drop below 35mm before the end of May, even if the pitch looks short. The grass needs the extra leaf area to recover from winter damage.

If growth is very slow (cold spring), keep the height at 40mm until the grass is actively growing. Do not mow when the grass is wet – this causes clumping and scalping.

5.3 Summer Mowing Heights (June – August)

Summer mowing is the most frequent, with the height reduced slightly for a faster, truer surface.

- June: 32mm
- July: 30mm
- August: 30mm

Mow every 3-4 days in summer, or twice a week if growth is strong. If the pitch is used for matches at the weekend, mow on Thursday or Friday, not the day before if possible. During dry spells, raise the height back to 35mm to reduce stress on the sward.

5.4 Autumn Mowing Heights (September – October)

As growth slows, raise the height gradually to prepare for winter.

- September: 32mm
- October: 38mm

Reduce mowing frequency to once a week or every 10 days. Stop mowing entirely when growth stops, usually late October, but if the grass is still growing in November, continue at 40mm.

5.5 Winter

No mowing from November to February unless the grass is unusually long (over 60mm). If a late autumn growth spurt occurs, mow at 45mm – this is the highest setting and helps prevent disease in the sward.

5.6 Mowing Patterns

Alternate the direction of mowing each session:

- Week 1: north-south
- Week 2: east-west
- Week 3: diagonal (from the north-east corner to the south-west corner)
- Week 4: repeat from week 1

Never mow in the same direction twice in a row. This prevents the grass from leaning and creates a more even surface. On match days, mow in the direction that gives the best visual stripe from the pavilion – usually north-south.

5.7 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.15 – "Height gauge was out of calibration – checked against a new one, off by 2mm. Recalibrated 12/04/19. J.B."
- p.15 – "Spring 2020 was very dry – kept at 40mm until late May, grass was stressed. J.B."
- p.16 – "Mower blades replaced 22/05/19 – new set, much cleaner cut. J.B."
**North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019**

**Section 6 – Line Marking**

6.1 General Principles

All line marking on the North Pitch is carried out by the grounds team. Match markings are
the responsibility of the home club for each fixture, but the pitch markings for league
matches are done by us as part of the standard service. Training lines are marked only when
requested by the coaching staff and must be removed before the next match.

The pitch is marked to the dimensions shown in Diagram 6A (attached). These follow the
current league regulations. If there is any doubt about a measurement, check the regulations
before painting. Do not guess.

6.2 Equipment

- Line marking machine: holds a 5-litre tank. Clean after every use – paint left in the
  nozzle will set and ruin the spray pattern.
- String line: 30m length, kept in the shed on the hook marked "LINE".
- Measuring tape: 50m, used for setting out. Do not use the tape for anything else.
- Paint: water-based, white, supplied in 10-litre drums. Store in the locked cabinet,
  not on the floor (damp gets in).
- Chalk: for temporary setting out. Do not leave chalk lines on the pitch overnight –
  they stain if it rains.

Handwritten note in margin (p.22):
"New string line ordered 14/03/19 – old one had stretched. J.B."

6.3 Setting Out

Setting out must be done in the following order:

1. Find the centre point of the pitch using the two diagonals. Peg the centre.
2. Mark the halfway line across the width.
3. Mark the centre circle (radius 9.15m) using a rope of the correct length tied to the
   centre peg.
4. Mark the penalty areas, goal areas, and penalty spots.
5. Mark the corner arcs (radius 1m) and the corner flags.
6. Mark the touchlines and goal lines last – these are the longest lines and are easiest
   to get straight once the internal markings are in place.

Do not rely on the previous week's markings. Always re-measure. Grass growth and
mowing can move the lines by a surprising amount over a week.

6.4 Painting

- Paint lines in two coats for match days. One coat is acceptable for training
  markings.
- The line width must be 100mm, no more and no less. The machine is set for this
  width – do not adjust it without checking with the Head Groundskeeper.
- Paint only when the grass is dry. Wet grass causes the paint to bleed and the line
  will look fuzzy.
- Do not paint in strong wind. The spray will drift and give a thin, uneven line.
- After painting, walk the line and check for gaps. Touch up any thin sections with a
  hand brush rather than re-running the machine.

6.5 Removing Old Markings

Old markings from the previous match should be removed before re-marking. Use the
following methods:

- If the old line is still visible, mow over it once in the same direction as the line.
  This usually lifts most of the paint.
- For stubborn lines, use the scarifier set to a shallow depth (3mm). Do not use the
  scarifier on a wet pitch.
- Do not use chemical paint removers on the pitch. They damage the sward.

**Section 7 – Weed Control**

7.1 Common Weeds on the North Pitch

The following weeds are commonly found on the North Pitch. Identification is important –
treating the wrong weed with the wrong product wastes money and can harm the grass.

- Daisies: very common, especially near the pavilion end where the soil is more
  compacted. White flowers, low growing.
- Plantain (ribwort): found in areas of poor drainage, particularly the south-east
  corner. Broad leaves, erect flower spikes.
- Dandelion: appears in spring, usually where the sward is thin. Yellow flowers,
  deep tap root.
- Clover: appears in dry summers. Can be beneficial in moderation, but if it covers
  more than 10% of the pitch it needs treatment.
- Moss: not a true weed, but treated in the same category. Appears in winter in
  shaded, damp areas. See Section 7.4.

7.2 Treatment Programme

Spring (March – May):

- Apply a selective weedkiller in late April, when the weeds are actively growing.
- Do not apply during a drought or when frost is forecast.
- Spot-treat individual weeds with a hand sprayer if the infestation is small.
- Do not apply weedkiller within 7 days of a match.

SOUTH PITCH MAINTENANCE MANUAL 2020

Grounds Department Reference: SP-MM-2020
Owner: Head Groundskeeper
Scope: South Pitch only (also referred to as South Field or Pitch 2)
Issued: March 2020
Review Cycle: Annual, with seasonal updates as noted

---

1. INTRODUCTION AND STATUS

South Pitch is the secondary grass pitch within the Merrowdale Sports Club complex, located on the south side of the clubhouse adjacent to the River Piddle flood meadow. It is used primarily for senior men's and women's training sessions, junior fixtures on Sunday mornings, and occasional midweek hire by external leagues.

This manual sets out the care standards for South Pitch and should be read alongside the North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2020 where common club-wide procedures apply. Where the two manuals differ, this document takes precedence for South Pitch.

Current drainage condition at time of issue:

South Pitch has_drainage_rating good. Record status: current.

This rating is current and reflects the condition following the winter works completed in February 2020. Any deterioration in drainage should be reported to the Head Groundskeeper without delay, particularly after sustained rainfall events or if standing water persists for more than 24 hours post-match.

Note: The drainage rating above supersedes the "fair" assessment recorded in the 2018 manual. The improvement is attributed to the installation of additional lateral drains along the western boundary and the clearing of the outfall into the River Piddle ditch.

2. PITCH SPECIFICATION

- Playing surface: Perennial ryegrass dominant sward
- Dimensions: 100m x 64m (including run-off areas)
- Mowing height (playing season): 28mm to 32mm
- Mowing height (winter): 35mm to 40mm
- Line marking: White, using water-based paint
- Goal areas: Standard 5.5m and 16.5m markings

3. SPRING MOW AND SEASONAL START-UP (MARCH – APRIL)

The spring mow programme begins once soil temperatures consistently exceed 8°C, typically in the second or third week of March. The following schedule applies:

- First cut: Reduce sward height gradually from winter height to 30mm over a two-week period. Do not remove more than one-third of leaf growth in a single cut.
- Subsequent cuts: Maintain at 30mm until the end of April, then reduce to 28mm for the main playing season.
- Frequency: Cut twice weekly during periods of active growth. Adjust to once weekly if growth slows due to dry weather.

Spring renovation works (to be completed by mid-April):

- Overseed any bare or thin areas using a ryegrass mix at 20g/m².
- Apply a spring fertiliser (e.g., 20:5:10 at 25g/m²) after the first cut.
- Drag a mat over the surface to lift lateral growth before the first full mow.

4. AERATION RECORDS

Aeration is critical for maintaining the drainage rating and reducing surface compaction. South Pitch receives aeration on the following schedule:

- Spring (April): Solid tine aeration to 100mm depth using 12mm tines, carried out when the soil is moist but not wet.
- Summer (June/July): Slit tine aeration to 75mm depth, particularly in high-traffic areas such as goal mouths and the centre circle.
- Autumn (September): Hollow tine aeration to 150mm depth, with cores removed and top-dressed with a 70/30 sand/soil mix.
- Winter (December/January): Deep spiking to 200mm depth using a vertidrain, weather and ground conditions permitting. Do not undertake deep spiking if the ground is frozen or waterlogged.

Aeration must be recorded in the Grounds Log Book after each operation, including date, depth, tine type, and weather conditions. Any areas that remain compacted after aeration should be flagged for repeat treatment within two weeks.

5. DRAINAGE INSPECTIONS

Regular drainage inspections are essential to maintaining the good rating noted above. Inspections should be carried out:

- Monthly during the playing season (April to October)
- Fortnightly during November to March, or after any rainfall event exceeding 20mm in 24 hours
- Immediately after any flooding incident
- Check all surface water gullies and ensure they are not covered by leaf fall or debris.
- Verify that the outfall pipe at the south-west corner is discharging freely into the River Piddle. If the river level is high, note whether the outfall is submerged.
- Inspect the access covers for the main drainage runs. Ensure they are flush with the surrounding surface and not a trip hazard.
- Look for any signs of lateral water movement across the surface, which may indicate a blocked or damaged lateral drain.

Red annotation (handwritten in margin, dated 22/11/20): Check the outfall at south-west after the November floods. It was slow to clear this year. The grate had silt up to the top edge. Will need clearing again before spring.

Any drainage defect found during inspections should be reported on the Grounds Defect Report form (GD-1) and handed to the Head Groundskeeper within two working days. Do not attempt to repair drains yourself unless you have received specific training and authorisation.

---

6. AERATION PROGRAMME 2020

Aeration is critical for maintaining the drainage rating and reducing surface compaction. South Pitch receives aeration on the following schedule:

Table 1 – Aeration dates and operations (2020)

| Operation | Target Date | Tine Type | Depth | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Spring aeration | w/c 20 April | Solid tine (12mm) | 100mm | Soil must be moist but not wet. Do not aerate if the surface is saturated. |
| Summer aeration | w/c 15 June | Slit tine (solid) | 75mm | Focus on goal mouths, the centre circle, and the main run-off area in front of the pavilion. |
| Autumn aeration | w/c 14 September | Hollow tine | 150mm | Cores to be removed and collected. Top-dress after aeration (see Section 7). |
| Winter deep spiking | w/c 4 January (completed 8 January) | Vertidrain (deep spiker) | 200mm | Completed. Ground conditions were suitable. See Grounds Log Book entry 12/01/20. |
| Winter deep spiking (second pass) | w/c 7 December | Vertidrain (deep spiker) | 200mm | Weather and ground conditions permitting. Do not undertake if frozen or waterlogged. |

The South Pitch Maintenance Manual 2020 states that the aeration frequency is twice per year. Record status: current. This is the current standard and applies to the core programme of solid tine and hollow tine work. The winter deep spiking is an additional operation that was introduced in 2019 to address the compaction issues around the goal mouths; it is not counted within the twice-yearly figure but should be carried out as scheduled to maintain the playing surface standard.

Aeration must be recorded in the Grounds Log Book after each operation, including date, depth, tine type, and weather conditions. Any areas that remain compacted after aeration should be flagged for repeat treatment within two weeks.

Red annotation (handwritten in margin, dated 02/06/20): Note – the June slit tining was delayed by one week due to the England match at the club. The pitch was closed for hire on the Sunday, so we moved the work to the Monday. Recorded in the log book as 22 June.

---

7. TOP DRESSING

Top dressing is carried out in conjunction with the autumn aeration programme. The purpose is to improve the soil profile, level minor undulations, and assist with thatch control.

Specification:

- Mix: 70/30 sand/soil blend (by volume). The sand should be a medium-coarse, lime-free, rootzone sand. The soil component should be a screened loam, free from stones and weed seeds.
- Application rate: 4–6 tonnes per 1000m². For the full South Pitch (approximately 7,200m²), this equates to 30–43 tonnes per application.
- Timing: Apply immediately after hollow tine aeration, while the tine holes are still open. Do not top dress when the surface is wet or when rain is forecast within 24 hours.
- Method: Spread evenly using a top dresser or by hand barrowing and raking. Brush the material into the holes using a drag mat or a stiff brush. Do not leave visible piles of material on the surface.
- Aftercare: Lightly roll the pitch after top dressing to settle the material. Do not mow for at least 48 hours, or until the surface has dried sufficiently.

The Pavilion is the oldest building on the club site. It was built in 1985, and although the club has grown around it, the original structure remains largely intact. The Pavilion Maintenance Manual 2021 notes that the Pavilion Building's construction year is 1985, and this remains the baseline for all maintenance planning. In practice this means that wiring, plumbing, and the roof structure are all of that era, and replacements should be specified to match current building regs, not the original installation. Do not assume that any part of the building is newer than it looks; several sections have been refurbished at different times and the dates are listed in Appendix B.

SECTION 2 – CLEANING SCHEDULES

Cleaning is shared between paid staff and volunteer rota. The Facilities Officer is responsible for checking that the schedule has been followed and for restocking cleaning materials.

Daily tasks (every day the Pavilion is open, including match days and event days):
- Sweep and spot-mop the main hall and corridor floors. Pay attention to the entrance mat well; it collects mud and grit.
- Wipe down the kitchen work surfaces with anti-bacterial spray. Do not use the same cloth for surfaces and the sink.
- Empty all bins into the wheelie bins outside the kitchen door. Replace bin bags. If a bin is not full, still check for food waste; in summer, fruit flies breed quickly.
- Clean the toilets: wipe the seats, flush handles, and taps; check hand soap and paper towel dispensers; report any empty dispensers to the Facilities Officer.
- Check the first aid box in the kitchen (small green box, top shelf) for missing items. Do not remove items without logging in the red book next to the box.

Weekly tasks (usually done on Monday mornings, unless a bank holiday, then Tuesday):
- Mop all hard floors with the diluted floor cleaner (see the label on the concentrate bottle in the cleaning cupboard).
- Vacuum the carpeted areas in the offices and the committee room. The vacuum cleaner is stored in the cleaning cupboard; the bag should be changed when the indicator shows red.
- Clean the inside of the kitchen microwave and the outside of the fridge and freezer.
- Wipe down the changing room benches and lockers with the disinfectant spray. Report any damaged lockers to the Facilities Officer.
- Clean the interior of the window in the main door and the fanlight above the kitchen door.

documents.content:
SECTION 3 – BOILER AND HEATING SYSTEM

3.1 General

The pavilion is heated by a Worcester Greenstar 24i combi boiler, installed in the plant cupboard off the main corridor. The boiler supplies radiators in the main hall, committee room, offices, and both changing rooms, and also provides hot water to the kitchen and toilets. The boiler is not to be touched by volunteers or visiting teams. Only the Facilities Officer, the club's named gas engineer, or a Gas Safe registered engineer may work on it.

The current gas engineer used by the club is P. Hensley (Merrowdale Heating Services), telephone 01305 749 118. He has serviced the boiler since 2018. The boiler service is due every September, before the heating season begins. The service record book is kept on the shelf above the boiler, in a clear plastic folder.

3.2 Boiler controls

The boiler has a simple dial thermostat on the wall of the main corridor, near the plant cupboard door. The dial is marked in numbers from 1 to 5, not in degrees. Normal winter setting is 3. Do not turn the dial above 4; the radiators in the main hall become too hot and the committee room overheats. In mild weather (October and April), setting 2 is usually enough.

There is a timer switch on the wall next to the thermostat. The timer is set as follows:

| Period | Setting |
|--------|---------|
| Weekdays, Sept–May | On 06:00–09:00 and 16:00–22:00 |
| Weekends and bank holidays, Sept–May | On 07:00–11:00 and 15:00–22:00 |
| June–August | Off, except when the hall is booked for events. For events, set to "On" manually and turn off at the end of the day. |

The timer is a mechanical type with pins. If the time shown is wrong after a power cut, reset it using the small dial behind the front cover. Do not force the pins; they are plastic and break easily. A replacement timer is kept in the plant cupboard, in the box marked "spares".

Pavilion Maintenance Manual 2021 last_reviewed 2021-11-30 date. Record status: superseded.

3.3 Pressure and bleeding

The boiler pressure gauge is on the front of the boiler, behind the drop-down flap. Normal pressure when the system is cold is between 1 and 1.5 bar. If the pressure drops below 1 bar, top up using the grey filling loop underneath the boiler. The filling loop valve should be closed again after topping up. If the pressure keeps dropping, do not keep topping up; report it to the Facilities Officer, as there may be a leak.

Radiators should be bled at the start of the heating season (usually the first week of October) and again in January if any radiator is cold at the top. Use the bleed key stored on the hook inside the plant cupboard door. Hold a cloth under the bleed valve before opening it, as water may spurt out. Close the valve as soon as water comes out steadily.

3.4 Fault finding and reporting

If the boiler fails to light, first check that the gas supply is on (the isolation valve on the pipe next to the boiler should be in line with the pipe) and that the timer is calling for heat. Then check the pressure gauge. If the boiler display shows an error code, note the code and the time it appeared, and call P. Hensley. Do not press the reset button more than twice in one day; repeated resetting can hide a real fault and may cause damage.

The following faults have been seen before and are noted here for reference:

| Fault | Likely cause | Action |
|-------|--------------|--------|
| Boiler lights, then goes out after a few minutes | Blocked condensate pipe (usually in cold weather) | Check the external pipe for ice; pour warm (not boiling) water over it. If it recurs, call the engineer. |
| Radiators hot at the bottom, cold at the top | Air in the system | Bleed the radiator. |
| Banging or gurgling noise from the boiler | Low pressure or trapped air | Check pressure; bleed radiators. If noise continues, call the engineer. |
| No hot water, but radiators heat up | Faulty diverter valve | Call the engineer. This has happened twice, in 2019 and 2020. |

Pavilion Maintenance Manual 2021

**Section 4: Windows, Guttering and Pest Control**

**4.1 Window cleaning**

Windows at the pavilion are to be cleaned internally and externally at least once a month from March to October, and once every six weeks from November to February. The schedule is set out in the Facilities calendar on the noticeboard in the plant cupboard.

Use the following products, stored in the locked cleaning cupboard in the annex:

- Glass cleaner (supplied by County Supplies, order code GL-114)
- Microfibre cloths (blue for glass, yellow for frames)
- Squeegee with rubber blade (long handle for upper panes)

Do not use abrasive pads or any cleaner containing bleach on the aluminium frames. The frames are powder-coated and bleach will mark them. Where frames have been repainted (see note in Appendix C), use only the mild soap solution described in Section 2.4.

Ladder use: the step ladder in the store is for internal window cleaning only. The extension ladder is kept in the external store behind the kitchen door and must only be used by two people. One person to foot the ladder at all times. Do not work from the ladder at the top of the fire escape; the ground is uneven there and the ladder will not sit level. For the high window over the main entrance, use the window pole with the squeegee attachment rather than climbing.

Report any cracked or broken panes immediately to the Facilities Officer. Do not attempt to remove broken glass yourself. Temporary boarding is kept in the store (two sheets of 6mm ply, marked "WINDOW BOARD").

**4.2 Gutter clearance**

Gutters and downpipes are to be cleared of leaves and debris twice a year: once in late autumn (usually the second week of November) and once in early spring (usually the third week of March). The exact dates are set by the Grounds Staff and will be written in the weekly task list.

The spring clearance is the more important of the two. The oak tree by the car park drops catkins in early April, and these block the downpipe at the corner nearest the tree. If the downpipe blocks, water overflows and runs down the side of the pavilion wall, which has caused damp in the past.

Method:

1. From the ground, use the gutter scoop on the extending pole to remove loose debris.
2. For the sections above the flat roof of the annex, use the ladder from the external store. Do not stand on the flat roof; the felt is not rated for foot traffic.
3. Flush the downpipes with a hose from the top, checking that water runs freely from the outlet at ground level.
4. Check the outlet at ground level is clear of leaves and that the gully grid is in place.

If a downpipe is found to be cracked or leaking at a joint, mark the location with tape and report it. Do not attempt to seal leaks with silicone from the store; the correct repair is a new section of pipe, which the Facilities Officer will arrange.

The gutter above the kitchen has been repaired twice (2019 and 2020) at the joint near the extractor fan outlet. This joint is prone to working loose in high winds. Check this joint specifically at each clearance and after any storm with wind speeds above 40mph (the Met Office warnings are usually enough of a prompt).

**4.3 Pest control**

The pavilion has a pest control contract with Dorset Pest Services (contract number DPS-221, renewed annually in April). The contract covers the building interior and the immediate exterior, including the bin store.

Routine monitoring:

- Mouse traps are set in the plant cupboard, the kitchen, and the store room. These are checked weekly by the Cleaner (normally a Thursday). The Cleaner initials the trap check sheet, which is kept in the back of the cleaning folder.
- Wasp nests: if a nest is reported, do not attempt to remove it. The contractor will attend within 48 hours. The nest at the top of the fire escape (reported July 2020) was treated and removed; the wasps have not returned.
- Pigeons: the roof of the annex is a known roosting spot. The bird spikes on the annex roof edge were replaced in March 2021 and are holding up well. If pigeons are seen entering the roof void, report it; there is a gap in the soffit on the east side that the Facilities Officer has ordered a repair for.

documents.title: North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019
documents.content:
The pitch is mown twice per week during the playing season, normally Tuesday and Friday
morning, weather permitting. Cut height is set at:

- Spring (March – May): 30mm
- Summer (June – August): 25mm
- Early autumn (September – October): 30mm

The final cut of the week (Friday) should be lower than the Tuesday cut by 2mm to allow for
growth over the weekend. If the pitch is waterlogged, do not mow. Mowing wet grass will
pull the sward and leave ruts.

Mowing pattern should alternate each cut:

- Week A: North–South (lengthways)
- Week B: East–West (widthways)

Do not mow the same direction twice in a row. This prevents grain and helps the grass stand
upright. The outfield (run-off) areas should be cut at 45mm, fortnightly.

2.2 Winter Mowing (November – February)

Mowing is reduced to once per week, or once every two weeks in very cold weather. Height is
raised to 40mm. Do not cut below 35mm during frost. If frost is forecast, stop mowing
48 hours beforehand where possible.

Winter mowing is for tidiness only – the grass will not be actively growing. If the pitch is
frozen solid, do not walk on it with mowers. Frost damage to the crown of the grass plant
can take until April to recover.

2.3 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.5 – "Spring cut 2019: started 12 March after dry week. J.B."
- p.5 – "Changed Friday cut to 28mm from 30mm on 3 May – grass growing fast. J.B."
- p.6 – "Winter cut 2018/19: only 14 cuts total. Mild but wet. J.B."

---

3. IRRIGATION SCHEDULE

3.1 Water Source and System

North Pitch is irrigated using a single pop-up sprinkler system fed from the club's borehole
(not the mains supply). The borehole is located behind the pavilion and is shared with the
bowls green. Water pressure varies with demand, so the sprinklers should not be run at the
same time as the bowls green irrigation.

The system has 12 pop-up heads, arranged in two banks of six. Bank A covers the northern
half, Bank B covers the southern half. Each bank runs for 20 minutes per cycle.

3.2 Irrigation Rules

North Pitch has_surface_type natural grass. Record status: current.

Irrigation is only permitted:

- Between 0600 and 0900 hours (to reduce evaporation)
- When the soil moisture deficit exceeds 15mm
- When wind speed is below 15 mph (check the anemometer at the pavilion)

Do not irrigate during rainfall or when rainfall is forecast within 6 hours. Do not irrigate
within 24 hours of a match unless the ground is exceptionally dry and the match official
has approved it.

3.3 Spring and Summer Schedule (April – September)

Irrigation is not usually required before mid-May unless there is a dry spell. The target is
to maintain moisture at a depth of 150mm. Use the soil probe to check – the top 25mm should
be dry but not dusty.

Typical schedule when irrigation is needed (dry spells only):

- Bank A: 0600, 0620, 0640 (20 min each)
- Bank B: 0700, 0720, 0740 (20 min each)

This gives a total of 60 minutes per bank per day, equivalent to approximately 8mm of
water. Do not exceed 12mm per day unless the pitch is newly seeded.

3.4 Autumn and Winter

Irrigation is stopped from October to March. The sprinkler heads must be drained and blown
through with compressed air before the first frost. This is a two-person job – see the
Winterisation Checklist (Appendix C).

3.5 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.9 – "Borehole pump replaced 14/05/19 – pressure much better. J.B."
- p.9 – "Irrigation needed only 4 times in June 2019 – wet month. J.B."
- p.10 – "Winterisation done 24/10/19. Heads drained OK. J.B."

---

4. FERTILIZER TYPES AND APPLICATION

4.1 General Principles

North Pitch receives three to four fertilizer applications per year. The aim is to maintain
a healthy sward without excessive growth. We do not use growth regulators – mowing is our
primary control.

All fertilizer must be stored in the locked chemical store (shed 2) and logged in the COSHH
register. Application records must be kept in the Fertilizer Log (Appendix D). Only
trained staff may apply fertilizer.

documents.title: North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019
documents.content:
Second application is usually June, only if the sward looks pale or the match schedule is heavy. Use a low-nitrogen feed:

- Product: 5-0-10 with iron
- Rate: 20g/m²
- Spreader setting: 10

Do not apply during a heatwave – if the forecast is above 25°C, wait for cooler weather. The iron helps with moss suppression but can stain the mower decks, so wash down after use.

4.4 Autumn Application

Third application is September/October. This is the most important one for root growth over winter.

- Product: 10-0-20 (high potash)
- Rate: 30g/m²
- Spreader setting: 14

Apply before the end of October. If the ground is very wet, use the pedestrian spreader instead of the tractor-mounted one to avoid rutting.

4.5 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

- p.12 – "Tried the 9-7-7 at 30g in April 2020 – too much, scorched the edges near the car park. Stick to 25g. J.B."
- p.12 – "June feed skipped in 2021 – pitch was green enough. Saved a bag. J.B."
- p.13 – "Autumn feed went on late 24/10/23 – fine, no frost yet. M.W."

---

5. MOWING PATTERNS AND HEIGHTS

5.1 General Principles

North Pitch is mown throughout the growing season, typically March to October. The aim is a playing surface of consistent height, with no scalping on the slopes and no build-up of thatch. All mowing must be recorded in the Mowing Log (Appendix E), including date, height, and any problems encountered.

Mowing heights are measured from the cutting edge to the ground, with the mower on a hard level surface. Check the height with a depth gauge before each mowing session – do not rely on the mower's own scale alone.

5.2 Spring Mowing Heights (March – May)

Spring mowing starts when the grass begins to grow, usually mid-March. Start higher than the summer height and reduce gradually as growth picks up.

- Early spring (March): 40mm
- Mid-spring (April): 38mm
- Late spring (May): 35mm

North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019 mowing_height_spring 35 mm. Record status: current. This is the standard spring height and is current – it has not changed since the manual was first issued. Do not drop below 35mm before the end of May, even if the pitch looks short. The grass needs the extra leaf area to recover from winter damage.

If growth is very slow (cold spring), keep the height at 40mm until the grass is actively growing. Do not mow when the grass is wet – this causes clumping and scalping.

5.3 Summer Mowing Heights (June – August)

Summer mowing is the most frequent, with the height reduced slightly for a faster, truer surface.

- June: 32mm
- July: 30mm
- August: 30mm

Mow every 3-4 days in summer, or twice a week if growth is strong. If the pitch is used for matches at the weekend, mow on Thursday or Friday, not the day before if possible. During dry spells, raise the height back to 35mm to reduce stress on the sward.

5.4 Autumn Mowing Heights (September – October)

As growth slows, raise the height gradually to prepare for winter.

- September: 32mm
- October: 38mm

Reduce mowing frequency to once a week or every 10 days. Stop mowing entirely when growth stops, usually late October, but if the grass is still growing in November, continue at 40mm.

5.5 Winter

No mowing from November to February unless the grass is unusually long (over 60mm). If a late autumn growth spurt occurs, mow at 45mm – this is the highest setting and helps prevent disease in the sward.

5.6 Mowing Patterns

Alternate the direction of mowing each session:

- Week 1: north-south
- Week 2: east-west
- Week 3: diagonal (from the north-east corner to the south-west corner)
- Week 4: repeat from week 1

Never mow in the same direction twice in a row. This prevents the grass from leaning and creates a more even surface. On match days, mow in the direction that gives the best visual stripe from the pavilion – usually north-south.

5.7 Marginal Notes (handwritten)

**North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2019**

**Section 6 – Line Marking**

6.1 General Principles

All line marking on the North Pitch is carried out by the grounds team. Match markings are
the responsibility of the home club for each fixture, but the pitch markings for league
matches are done by us as part of the standard service. Training lines are marked only when
requested by the coaching staff and must be removed before the next match.

The pitch is marked to the dimensions shown in Diagram 6A (attached). These follow the
current league regulations. If there is any doubt about a measurement, check the regulations
before painting. Do not guess.

6.2 Equipment

- Line marking machine: holds a 5-litre tank. Clean after every use – paint left in the
  nozzle will set and ruin the spray pattern.
- String line: 30m length, kept in the shed on the hook marked "LINE".
- Measuring tape: 50m, used for setting out. Do not use the tape for anything else.
- Paint: water-based, white, supplied in 10-litre drums. Store in the locked cabinet,
  not on the floor (damp gets in).
- Chalk: for temporary setting out. Do not leave chalk lines on the pitch overnight –
  they stain if it rains.

Handwritten note in margin (p.22):
"New string line ordered 14/03/19 – old one had stretched. J.B."

6.3 Setting Out

Setting out must be done in the following order:

1. Find the centre point of the pitch using the two diagonals. Peg the centre.
2. Mark the halfway line across the width.
3. Mark the centre circle (radius 9.15m) using a rope of the correct length tied to the
   centre peg.
4. Mark the penalty areas, goal areas, and penalty spots.
5. Mark the corner arcs (radius 1m) and the corner flags.
6. Mark the touchlines and goal lines last – these are the longest lines and are easiest
   to get straight once the internal markings are in place.

Do not rely on the previous week's markings. Always re-measure. Grass growth and
mowing can move the lines by a surprising amount over a week.

6.4 Painting

- Paint lines in two coats for match days. One coat is acceptable for training
  markings.
- The line width must be 100mm, no more and no less. The machine is set for this
  width – do not adjust it without checking with the Head Groundskeeper.
- Paint only when the grass is dry. Wet grass causes the paint to bleed and the line
  will look fuzzy.
- Do not paint in strong wind. The spray will drift and give a thin, uneven line.
- After painting, walk the line and check for gaps. Touch up any thin sections with a
  hand brush rather than re-running the machine.

6.5 Removing Old Markings

Old markings from the previous match should be removed before re-marking. Use the
following methods:

- If the old line is still visible, mow over it once in the same direction as the line.
  This usually lifts most of the paint.
- For stubborn lines, use the scarifier set to a shallow depth (3mm). Do not use the
  scarifier on a wet pitch.
- Do not use chemical paint removers on the pitch. They damage the sward.

**Section 7 – Weed Control**

7.1 Common Weeds on the North Pitch

The following weeds are commonly found on the North Pitch. Identification is important –
treating the wrong weed with the wrong product wastes money and can harm the grass.

- Daisies: very common, especially near the pavilion end where the soil is more
  compacted. White flowers, low growing.
- Plantain (ribwort): found in areas of poor drainage, particularly the south-east
  corner. Broad leaves, erect flower spikes.
- Dandelion: appears in spring, usually where the sward is thin. Yellow flowers,
  deep tap root.
- Clover: appears in dry summers. Can be beneficial in moderation, but if it covers
  more than 10% of the pitch it needs treatment.
- Moss: not a true weed, but treated in the same category. Appears in winter in
  shaded, damp areas. See Section 7.4.

7.2 Treatment Programme

Spring (March – May):

- Apply a selective weedkiller in late April, when the weeds are actively growing.
- Do not apply during a drought or when frost is forecast.
- Spot-treat individual weeds with a hand sprayer if the infestation is small.
- Do not apply weedkiller within 7 days of a match.

documents.content:
SOUTH PITCH MAINTENANCE MANUAL 2020

Grounds Department Reference: SP-MM-2020
Owner: Head Groundskeeper
Scope: South Pitch only (also referred to as South Field or Pitch 2)
Issued: March 2020
Review Cycle: Annual, with seasonal updates as noted

---

1. INTRODUCTION AND STATUS

South Pitch is the secondary grass pitch within the Merrowdale Sports Club complex, located on the south side of the clubhouse adjacent to the River Piddle flood meadow. It is used primarily for senior men's and women's training sessions, junior fixtures on Sunday mornings, and occasional midweek hire by external leagues.

This manual sets out the care standards for South Pitch and should be read alongside the North Pitch Maintenance Manual 2020 where common club-wide procedures apply. Where the two manuals differ, this document takes precedence for South Pitch.

Current drainage condition at time of issue:

South Pitch has_drainage_rating good. Record status: current.

This rating is current and reflects the condition following the winter works completed in February 2020. Any deterioration in drainage should be reported to the Head Groundskeeper without delay, particularly after sustained rainfall events or if standing water persists for more than 24 hours post-match.

Note: The drainage rating above supersedes the "fair" assessment recorded in the 2018 manual. The improvement is attributed to the installation of additional lateral drains along the western boundary and the clearing of the outfall into the River Piddle ditch.

2. PITCH SPECIFICATION

- Playing surface: Perennial ryegrass dominant sward
- Dimensions: 100m x 64m (including run-off areas)
- Mowing height (playing season): 28mm to 32mm
- Mowing height (winter): 35mm to 40mm
- Line marking: White, using water-based paint
- Goal areas: Standard 5.5m and 16.5m markings

3. SPRING MOW AND SEASONAL START-UP (MARCH – APRIL)

The spring mow programme begins once soil temperatures consistently exceed 8°C, typically in the second or third week of March. The following schedule applies:

- First cut: Reduce sward height gradually from winter height to 30mm over a two-week period. Do not remove more than one-third of leaf growth in a single cut.
- Subsequent cuts: Maintain at 30mm until the end of April, then reduce to 28mm for the main playing season.
- Frequency: Cut twice weekly during periods of active growth. Adjust to once weekly if growth slows due to dry weather.

Spring renovation works (to be completed by mid-April):

- Overseed any bare or thin areas using a ryegrass mix at 20g/m².
- Apply a spring fertiliser (e.g., 20:5:10 at 25g/m²) after the first cut.
- Drag a mat over the surface to lift lateral growth before the first full mow.

4. AERATION RECORDS

Aeration is critical for maintaining the drainage rating and reducing surface compaction. South Pitch receives aeration on the following schedule:

- Spring (April): Solid tine aeration to 100mm depth using 12mm tines, carried out when the soil is moist but not wet.
- Summer (June/July): Slit tine aeration to 75mm depth, particularly in high-traffic areas such as goal mouths and the centre circle.
- Autumn (September): Hollow tine aeration to 150mm depth, with cores removed and top-dressed with a 70/30 sand/soil mix.
- Winter (December/January): Deep spiking to 200mm depth using a vertidrain, weather and ground conditions permitting. Do not undertake deep spiking if the ground is frozen or waterlogged.

Aeration must be recorded in the Grounds Log Book after each operation, including date, depth, tine type, and weather conditions. Any areas that remain compacted after aeration should be flagged for repeat treatment within two weeks.

5. DRAINAGE INSPECTIONS

Regular drainage inspections are essential to maintaining the good rating noted above. Inspections should be carried out:

- Monthly during the playing season (April to October)
- Fortnightly during November to March, or after any rainfall event exceeding 20mm in 24 hours
- Immediately after any flooding incident

- Check all surface water gullies and ensure they are not covered by leaf fall or debris.
- Verify that the outfall pipe at the south-west corner is discharging freely into the River Piddle. If the river level is high, note whether the outfall is submerged.
- Inspect the access covers for the main drainage runs. Ensure they are flush with the surrounding surface and not a trip hazard.
- Look for any signs of lateral water movement across the surface, which may indicate a blocked or damaged lateral drain.

Red annotation (handwritten in margin, dated 22/11/20): Check the outfall at south-west after the November floods. It was slow to clear this year. The grate had silt up to the top edge. Will need clearing again before spring.

Any drainage defect found during inspections should be reported on the Grounds Defect Report form (GD-1) and handed to the Head Groundskeeper within two working days. Do not attempt to repair drains yourself unless you have received specific training and authorisation.

---

6. AERATION PROGRAMME 2020

Aeration is critical for maintaining the drainage rating and reducing surface compaction. South Pitch receives aeration on the following schedule:

Table 1 – Aeration dates and operations (2020)

| Operation | Target Date | Tine Type | Depth | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Spring aeration | w/c 20 April | Solid tine (12mm) | 100mm | Soil must be moist but not wet. Do not aerate if the surface is saturated. |
| Summer aeration | w/c 15 June | Slit tine (solid) | 75mm | Focus on goal mouths, the centre circle, and the main run-off area in front of the pavilion. |
| Autumn aeration | w/c 14 September | Hollow tine | 150mm | Cores to be removed and collected. Top-dress after aeration (see Section 7). |
| Winter deep spiking | w/c 4 January (completed 8 January) | Vertidrain (deep spiker) | 200mm | Completed. Ground conditions were suitable. See Grounds Log Book entry 12/01/20. |
| Winter deep spiking (second pass) | w/c 7 December | Vertidrain (deep spiker) | 200mm | Weather and ground conditions permitting. Do not undertake if frozen or waterlogged. |

The South Pitch Maintenance Manual 2020 states that the aeration frequency is twice per year. Record status: current. This is the current standard and applies to the core programme of solid tine and hollow tine work. The winter deep spiking is an additional operation that was introduced in 2019 to address the compaction issues around the goal mouths; it is not counted within the twice-yearly figure but should be carried out as scheduled to maintain the playing surface standard.

Aeration must be recorded in the Grounds Log Book after each operation, including date, depth, tine type, and weather conditions. Any areas that remain compacted after aeration should be flagged for repeat treatment within two weeks.

Red annotation (handwritten in margin, dated 02/06/20): Note – the June slit tining was delayed by one week due to the England match at the club. The pitch was closed for hire on the Sunday, so we moved the work to the Monday. Recorded in the log book as 22 June.

---

7. TOP DRESSING

Top dressing is carried out in conjunction with the autumn aeration programme. The purpose is to improve the soil profile, level minor undulations, and assist with thatch control.

Specification:

- Mix: 70/30 sand/soil blend (by volume). The sand should be a medium-coarse, lime-free, rootzone sand. The soil component should be a screened loam, free from stones and weed seeds.
- Application rate: 4–6 tonnes per 1000m². For the full South Pitch (approximately 7,200m²), this equates to 30–43 tonnes per application.
- Timing: Apply immediately after hollow tine aeration, while the tine holes are still open. Do not top dress when the surface is wet or when rain is forecast within 24 hours.
- Method: Spread evenly using a top dresser or by hand barrowing and raking. Brush the material into the holes using a drag mat or a stiff brush. Do not leave visible piles of material on the surface.
- Aftercare: Lightly roll the pitch after top dressing to settle the material. Do not mow for at least 48 hours, or until the surface has dried sufficiently.
